review_note: Preserves the three standard-cover Čech facts: finite disjoint union V→U is a τ-covering, original finite family refines singleton, and induced cochain maps for arbitrary abelian sheaf are degreewise isomorphisms.
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and choose either (a) the big $\tau$ site $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{fppf},\mathrm{\acute etale},\mathrm{smooth},\mathrm{syntomic}\}$, (b) the small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$, or (c) the small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. Let $U$ be an affine object of that site and let $\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i=1}^n$ be a standard affine $\tau$-covering, with all $U_i$ affine. For any abelian sheaf $\mathcal F$ on that site, put $V=\coprod_iU_i$ and $\mathcal V=\{V\to U\}$. Then $\mathcal V$ is a $\tau$-covering, $\mathcal U$ refines $\mathcal V$, and the canonical refinement morphism of Čech cochain complexes $\check C^\bullet(\mathcal V,\mathcal F)\to\check C^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is an isomorphism in every degree, using the standard fibre-product intersections and the product decomposition for sections on finite disjoint unions.
hypotheses: C is one of the eligible big/small sites; U is affine; U_i are an affine standard finite tau covering; F is an abelian sheaf.
conclusions: Replacing a finite covering by its coproduct gives a covering with isomorphic Čech complexes.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-covering-Cech}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] fppf, \linebreak[0]
\etale, \linebreak[0] smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic\}$
and $\mathcal{C} = (\Sch/S)_\tau$, or
\item[(b)] let $\tau = \etale$ and $\mathcal{C} = S_\etale$, or
\item[(c)] let $\tau = Zariski$ and $\mathcal{C} = S_{Zar}$.
\end{enumerate}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an abelian sheaf on $\mathcal{C}$.
Let $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ be affine.
Let $\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i = 1, \ldots, n}$ be a standard affine
$\tau$-covering in $\mathcal{C}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{V} = \{\coprod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} U_i \to U\}$ is a
$\tau$-covering of $U$,
\item $\mathcal{U}$ is a refinement of $\mathcal{V}$, and
\item the induced map on {\v C}ech complexes
(Cohomology on Sites,
Equation (\ref{sites-cohomology-equation-map-cech-complexes}))
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{F})
\longrightarrow
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F})
$$
is an isomorphism of complexes.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Retains the identification of Čech cochain complex of standard affine τ-cover with the Amitsur complex for faithfully flat R→∏Γ(U_i,O), plus all positive Čech cohomology vanishing for qc F.
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\tau,\mathcal C,U,\mathcal U=\{U_i\to U\}_{i=1}^n$ be as follows: $\mathcal C$ is one of the big Zariski, fppf, étale, smooth or syntomic sites over $S$, or the small Zariski or étale site; $U$ and all $U_i$ are affine and $\mathcal U$ is a standard affine covering in $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$, put $R=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, $V=\coprod_iU_i=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $A=\prod_i\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})$, and $M=\Gamma(U,\mathcal F^a)$. The map $R\to A$ is faithfully flat. With $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal F|_T)$, the Čech complex of $\mathcal U$ with coefficients in $\mathcal F^a$ is canonically isomorphic to the unaugmented Amitsur cochain complex
$$A\otimes_RM\to A^{\otimes_R2}\otimes_RM\to A^{\otimes_R3}\otimes_RM\to\cdots$$
whose differential is the alternating sum of insertion-of-unit maps. In particular, $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F^a)=0$ for all $p\geq1$.
hypotheses: Finite standard affine site covering of affine U; F quasi-coherent on S.
conclusions: Čech complex identifies with unaugmented Amitsur complex, and higher Čech cohomology vanishes.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-standard-covering-Cech-quasi-coherent}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$.
Let $\tau$, $\mathcal{C}$, $U$, $\mathcal{U}$ be as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-standard-covering-Cech}. Then there is an isomorphism
of complexes
$$
\check{\mathcal{C}}^\bullet(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}^a)
\cong
s((A/R)_\bullet \otimes_R M)
$$
(see Section \ref{section-descent-modules})
where $R = \Gamma(U, \mathcal{O}_U)$, $M = \Gamma(U, \mathcal{F}^a)$
and $R \to A$ is a faithfully flat ring map. In particular
$$
\check{H}^p(\mathcal{U}, \mathcal{F}^a) = 0
$$
for all $p \geq 1$.

review_note: Preserves topology independence H^q(S,F) for qc F and big Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, fppf sites, along with small Zariski and étale; asserts only cohomology groups, not arbitrary sheaves.
statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). For every $q\geq0$, there is a canonical isomorphism $H^q(S,\mathcal F)\cong H^q((\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau,\mathcal F^a)$ of sheaf-cohomology groups, for each $\tau$ in the five listed topologies. There are also canonical isomorphisms $H^q(S,\mathcal F)\cong H^q(S_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal F^a)\cong H^q(S_{\mathrm{\acute et}},\mathcal F^a)$.
hypotheses: F is quasi-coherent and tau an indicated topology.
conclusions: Sheaf cohomology agrees between the scheme, big tau site, and small Zariski/étale sites.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-same-cohomology-quasi-coherent}
\begin{slogan}
Cohomology of quasi-coherent sheaves is the same no matter which
topology you use.
\end{slogan}
Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $S$.
Let $\tau \in \{Zariski, \linebreak[0] \etale, \linebreak[0]
smooth, \linebreak[0] syntomic, \linebreak[0] fppf\}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a canonical isomorphism
$$
H^q(S, \mathcal{F}) = H^q((\Sch/S)_\tau, \mathcal{F}^a).
$$
\item There are canonical isomorphisms
$$
H^q(S, \mathcal{F}) =
H^q(S_{Zar}, \mathcal{F}^a) =
H^q(S_\etale, \mathcal{F}^a).
$$
\end{enumerate}

review_note: Preserves three functoriality clauses: all eligible site equivalences commute with pullback, big-site pushforward comparison is not generally valid, and small Zariski/étale qcqs pushforward (including higher direct-image context separately) commutes.
statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. (1) For every eligible $\tau$, passing from quasi-coherent sheaves to the associated big-site sheaves commutes with pullback, and the same holds on the small Zariski and étale sites: $f_{\mathrm{site}}^*(\mathcal G^a)\cong(f^*\mathcal G)^a$. (2) The analogous big-site pushforward compatibility is false in general (and $f_*$ need not preserve quasi-coherence). (3) If $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then for $\tau\in\{\mathrm{Zariski},\mathrm{\acute etale}\}$ both $f_*$ on schemes and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}$ on small sites preserve quasi-coherent sheaves, and $f_{\mathrm{small},*}(\mathcal F^a)\cong(f_*\mathcal F)^a$ for every quasi-coherent $\mathcal F$ on $T$.
hypotheses: f:T→S is a scheme morphism; qcqs is required for the small-site pushforward claim.
conclusions: Associated-sheaf equivalences commute with pullback; generally not with big-site pushforward; qcqs small-Zariski/étale pushforward is compatible.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent-functorial}
Let $f : T \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
\begin{enumerate}
\item The equivalences of categories of
Proposition \ref{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent}
are compatible with pullback.
More precisely, we have $f^*(\mathcal{G}^a) = (f^*\mathcal{G})^a$
for any quasi-coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}$ on $S$.
\item The equivalences of categories of
Proposition \ref{proposition-equivalence-quasi-coherent} part (1)
are {\bf not} compatible with pushforward in general.
\item If $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and
$\tau \in \{Zariski, \etale\}$ then $f_*$ and $f_{small, *}$
preserve quasi-coherent sheaves and the diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_T)
\ar[rr]_{f_*} \ar[d]_{\mathcal{F} \mapsto \mathcal{F}^a} & &
\QCoh(\mathcal{O}_S)
\ar[d]^{\mathcal{G} \mapsto \mathcal{G}^a} \\
\QCoh(T_\tau, \mathcal{O}) \ar[rr]^{f_{small, *}} & &
\QCoh(S_\tau, \mathcal{O})
}
$$
is commutative, i.e., $f_{small, *}(\mathcal{F}^a) = (f_*\mathcal{F})^a$.
\end{enumerate}

review_note: For qcqs f:T→S and qc F on T, retains canonical comparison R^i f_{small,*}(F^a)≅(R^i f_*F)^a in small Zariski or étale topology, for i≥0.
statement:
For $\tau$ among Zariski, étale, smooth, syntomic, and fppf, let $(\operatorname{Sch}/S)_\tau$ be the big site of all schemes over $S$ with the stated topology and structure sheaf $\mathcal O(T\to S)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. The small Zariski site $S_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and small étale site $S_{\mathrm{\acute et}}$ have as objects open immersions or étale morphisms to $S$, respectively, with the corresponding structure sheaf.
For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module $\mathcal F$, denote by $\mathcal F^a$ the $\mathcal O$-module on the indicated site given on each object $g:T\to S$ by $\mathcal F^a(T)=\Gamma(T,g^*\mathcal F)$ (restricted to the small site when appropriate). Let $f:T\to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes, let $\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent on $T$, and take $\tau$ to be the small Zariski or small étale topology. Then for every $i\geq0$ there is a canonical isomorphism of $\mathcal O$-modules on the small site $S_\tau$:
$$R^if_{\mathrm{small},*}(\mathcal F^a)\cong(R^if_*\mathcal F)^a.$$
hypotheses: f is qcqs, F is quasi-coherent, and tau is small Zariski or étale.
conclusions: Higher direct images commute with associating the small-site module.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-higher-direct-images-small-etale}
Let $f : T \to S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent sheaf on $T$. For either the \'etale
or Zariski topology, there are canonical isomorphisms
$R^if_{small, *}(\mathcal{F}^a) = (R^if_*\mathcal{F})^a$.
